title: Quantum powered credit risk assessment: a novel approach using Hybrid Quantum-Classical Deep Neural Network for Row-Type Dependent Predictive Analysis
abstract_summary: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical deep neural network framework (HyQuC-DeepNN-RTDPA) for credit risk assessment that applies Row-Type Dependent Predictive Analysis to tailor models for different loan categories. The method integrates quantum embedding and quantum layers with classical deep networks, addresses class imbalance with SMOTE, and is evaluated on a large bank dataset of agriculture and personal loans; results show reasonable overall accuracy but limited performance on minority classes due to simulator and hardware constraints. The study presents the framework, experimental findings, and discusses limitations (dimensionality reduction, hardware, interpretability) and directions for future work.
methodology_description: The study proposes a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Deep Neural Network for Row-Type Dependent Predictive Analysis (HyQuC-DeepNN-RTDPA). The authors partitioned the dataset by row-type (loan subcategories: Agriculture and Personal) and applied row-type-specific preprocessing (handling missing values, dropping features with >70% missing, removing non-applicable columns, consolidating rare classes). Dimensionality reduction was performed via PCA (originally targeting 43 components for personal and 38 for agriculture) but experiments used only the top 5 principal components due to quantum simulator limitations. Class imbalance was addressed with data augmentation techniques (SMOTE is cited). The predictive model architecture embeds classical features into a parameterized quantum circuit (angle embedding is used in the experiments; amplitude embedding is discussed as an alternative), applies entangling layers (e.g., StronglyEntanglingLayers), measures expectation values of Pauli-Z on qubits to produce a classical feature vector, and feeds those measurements into classical dense layers with softmax outputs. Training is performed per row type, with hyperparameter tuning via grid search (nlayers, nqubits, learning_rate, batch_size, nepochs) and cross-validation for selection of best hyperparameters. Quantum gradients are computed using the parameter-shift rule; classical parameters are updated via gradient-based optimizers. Performance is evaluated using standard classification metrics (precision, recall, F1, accuracy, ROC AUC) and Cohen's Kappa. The paper also documents an appendix walkthrough showing angle-encoding, rotation gates, measurement, classical processing, loss (binary cross-entropy example), and parameter-shift gradient calculation.

experiment_input: Source: internal bank dataset (xxx Bank). Size: >25,000 rows, 81 columns. Preprocessing per row-type: drop features not applicable (e.g., 'dryland'/'wetland' removed for personal loans), remove features with >70% missing, handle missing values, remove constant/unique-valued features, consolidate rare label classes, and apply SMOTE for minority-class augmentation. Dimensionality reduction: PCA applied yielding recommended components (43 for personal, 38 for agriculture) but only top 5 principal components were used in experiments due to quantum simulator capacity constraints.
experiment_process: Pipeline: (1) Partition dataset by row-type (RTDPA). (2) Row-type-specific preprocessing and class imbalance handling (SMOTE). (3) Dimensionality reduction via PCA and selection of top-k components (k=5 in experiments). (4) Quantum embedding of classical features using angle embedding into a parameterized quantum circuit (QNode). (5) Application of entangling layers (e.g., StronglyEntanglingLayers) to produce entangled quantum states. (6) Measurement: expectation values of Z on each qubit extracted to form classical feature vector. (7) Feed measurements into classical dense layers followed by softmax for classification. (8) Train per row-type; compute gradients using parameter-shift rule for quantum parameters and standard gradient-based updates for classical parameters. (9) Hyperparameter grid search over nlayers (e.g., 1–3), nqubits (e.g., 2–4), learning_rate (0.01, 0.001), batch_size (16, 32), nepochs (50, 100) with cross-validation to pick best configuration. (10) Evaluate final models on test splits. The appendix contains a worked numerical example using rotation gates and binary cross-entropy to illustrate forward/backward passes.
experiment_output: Outputs are classification predictions per loan row-type and a suite of performance metrics: train/validation/test accuracy, class-wise precision/recall/F1-score, macro and weighted averages, ROC AUC (per class), and Cohen's Kappa. Reported example results: Personal loans — overall accuracy ~0.8348; Agriculture loans — overall accuracy ~0.8112. Detailed class-level precision/recall/F1 and ROC AUC arrays are provided in the paper tables.

results_summary: This paper presents HyQuC-DeepNN-RTDPA, a hybrid quantum-classical deep learning framework for credit risk assessment that separates rows by loan type (RTDPA) and integrates quantum encoding and parameterized quantum layers with classical dense layers. Using a bank dataset of >25,000 records and 81 attributes, the authors performed PCA (nominally selecting 43 and 38 components) but restricted experiments to the first five principal components due to simulator/hardware constraints. The hybrid models produced test accuracies of ~0.8348 for personal loans and ~0.8112 for agriculture loans, with detailed per-class precision/recall/F1, ROC AUC and Cohen's Kappa reported. The study emphasizes conceptual benefits of quantum embedding and entangling layers for feature transformation, but does not present controlled comparisons to purely classical baselines or demonstrate a hardware quantum speedup. The authors describe important computational and methodological limitations and frame claims about quantum advantage and broader applicability as prospective rather than conclusively demonstrated.
